idiom_name: per-object role objects in a WeakMap registry; Object.assign or Proxy for transparent lookup
implementation_notes: JavaScript's object model is the pattern's runtime: behaviour can be attached to one object at a time with Object.assign or property assignment, and a role is just an object that wraps the core and forwards, so the language's native composition replaces the ComponentRole subclassing entirely. Keep the core as owner of its roles through a WeakMap keyed by the core, so role sets die with their subject and never become globals; when clients should not see the registry at all, wrap the core in a Proxy whose get trap checks role members before falling back to the core. The explicit class hierarchy is still justified when role state is large, roles are serialized, or a uniform add/get/remove/has protocol must be enforced across modules.
pitfalls: A WeakMap keyed by object identity means a spread or cloned core starts with an empty role set; keep one canonical core reference per subject.
Roles that close over the core and are stored on the core form cycles - harmless to mark-and-sweep GC, but they keep subjects alive if a role escapes into a long-lived collection.
Installing role methods directly on the core can silently overwrite core members with the same name; namespace role members or keep the role object separate.
